clue.text: A competition to fire people!

parts.note: to fire someone is to sack them from a job
a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: A jokey exclamation that a contest exists for firing staff.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark flags the fun: firing people sounds like a staff cull. A sack race is a children's sports-day event where runners hop along inside sacks.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a sports-day event where runners hop inside sacks, so it is a kind of contest.

clue.text: Train swimmers as a group

definitions.meaning: to train is to educate or teach
a large group of fish swimming together

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to educate or drill someone, and a shoal of fish.

clue.text: Covering wrapped around an appetiser

indicators.note: wrapped around says the covering word encloses the next piece

parts.note: a cape is a covering cloak
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wrapping folded round a small starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covering' looks like the definition, but the snack is the definition and the covering is a cloak.
explanation.definitionFit: A small savoury on bread or pastry served before a meal is an appetiser.

clue.text: Revolting individual getting a step up

definitions.meaning: someone who rises up in revolt, a rebel
the vertical part of a stair step

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both one who rises in rebellion and the upright board between treads of a staircase.

clue.text: Figure set in advance

indicators.note: in places the setting word within the advancing word

parts.note: to come is to advance or approach
to put is to set or place

explanation.surface: A number decided ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' reads as a noun and 'set in advance' as fixed beforehand, but PUT (set) goes 'in' COME (advance).
explanation.definitionFit: To figure out a sum is to calculate it.

clue.text: King Charles at the river hazardous situation

parts.note: CR stands for Carolus Rex, Latin for King Charles
the Isis is the name of the Thames at Oxford

explanation.surface: A king named Charles finds himself in danger beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: CR (Carolus Rex) is the royal cipher of King Charles; the ISIS is the stretch of the River Thames running through Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: A turning point of danger or difficulty is exactly a hazardous situation.

clue.text: Subdued and retiring creature cut by the crowd

indicators.note: cut by says the reversed word is split open with the crowd word inside
retiring means going back, so the creature word is read in reverse

parts.note: a deer is a creature, an animal
a press is a crowd or throng

explanation.surface: A shy animal is subdued when a crowd breaks through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' turns DEER into REED; 'cut by' opens it to hold PRESS (crowd).
explanation.definitionFit: Held down or kept in check means subdued.

clue.text: Stall on a short road? That's typical!

parts.note: a stand is a stall at a market or fair
taken as written
RD is the short form of road

explanation.surface: A roadside stall, found everywhere, as one would expect.
explanation.walkthrough: STAND (stall), then A and RD, the abbreviation for road.
explanation.definitionFit: Something normal or usual is standard, typical.

clue.text: Lady's tie knotted firmly

indicators.note: knotted signals that the letters of the lady's tie phrase are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman's necktie tied securely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knotted' rearranges the eight letters of LADYS TIE; the apostrophe adds nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something steadily means doing it firmly and without wavering.

clue.text: Fine sand may be used in the household

indicators.note: in signals that one piece is placed inside the household word

parts.note: a home is a household

indicators.note: the letters of sand may be used in another arrangement, so they are shuffled

explanation.surface: Fine-grained sand might find a use around the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be used' signals an anagram: SAND becomes ANDS, which goes 'in' HOME. 'Fine' looks like a description of the sand, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine and handsome both mean good-looking or generous, as in a fine figure or a handsome sum.

clue.text: Raise apprehension

definitions.meaning: a taking up or lifting, as of a substance absorbed or a pipe drawing air upwards
apprehension here is understanding, as in being quick on the take-up

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an act of taking up or lifting, and mental grasp or comprehension.

clue.text: Base for design

definitions.meaning: to design is to intend or have in mind

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both ignoble or miserly, and to intend or purpose.

clue.text: Work quietly or strain as appropriate

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
taken as written
a strain is a tune or melody

explanation.surface: Advice to a musician to play softly or carry a tune as suits the moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Something well-timed or suitable is apt and appropriate.

clue.text: Finished in less than the intended time

indicators.note: less than tells us to take some letters away from the word intended

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something completed sooner than the planned time.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as finishing early, but 'in' and 'time' (T) are both taken from INTENDED, leaving the definition's synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Something finished has come to an end, it is over.

clue.text: In the church space is reorganised after chapter leaves

definitions.note: the definition describes a part found in a church rather than naming it

indicators.note: is reorganised means the remaining letters are rearranged into a new order
the chapter abbreviation departs from the word space before the shuffle

explanation.surface: A church's floor plan is reworked once a chapter of clergy departs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after chapter leaves' removes C (chapter) from SPACE, leaving SPAE, and 'is reorganised' rearranges those four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the vaulted recess at the east end of a church, behind the altar, so it is a place in the church.

clue.text: Average lot, yet outstanding

parts.note: par is the normal or average level
a lot is an amount or quantity

explanation.surface: Ordinary stuff, and yet excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Supreme or pre-eminent means outstanding.

clue.text: Such a breathing-space is essential for everybody

definitions.text: Such a breathing-space is essential for everybody

parts.words: Such a breathing-space is essential for everybody
parts.note: breathing-space reads as a rest, but here is literally an opening in the nose for air that everyone needs

explanation.definitionFit: Each of the two openings in the nose is literally a space through which we breathe.

clue.text: Make notes about temporary accommodation not doing very well

indicators.note: about says the singing word goes round the other piece

parts.note: to sing is to make musical notes
a camp provides temporary shelter

explanation.surface: Jotting things down about a campsite that is not going well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make notes' suggests writing, but it is SING, which goes 'about' CAMP. To scamp work is to skimp or do it carelessly.
explanation.definitionFit: To scamp a job is to do it hastily and poorly, so not doing it well.

clue.text: Royalist archbishop is competent and praiseworthy

parts.note: William Laud was Archbishop of Canterbury under Charles I, a royalist executed in 1645
able means competent

explanation.surface: A churchman loyal to the Crown is capable and admirable.
explanation.walkthrough: William Laud was Charles I's Archbishop of Canterbury, a staunch royalist.
explanation.definitionFit: Deserving praise is the meaning of praiseworthy, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Smile after tea, occasioning some annoyance

indicators.note: after places the smile word following the tea word in the answer

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea
a grin is a broad smile

explanation.surface: A smile following the tea round causes some irritation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the smile second; the tea word is old British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Vexation or embarrassed disappointment is a form of annoyance.

clue.text: There's little point in 10 return some

indicators.note: in says a piece sits inside the turned number
return means the number word is turned backwards

parts.note: the number ten written as a word
S is the short form of south, a compass point

explanation.surface: There is little purpose in a few coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' looks like a cross-reference but is simply TEN; 'return' makes NET, with S (south, a point of the compass) 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest of tables is a set, a group of several, hence some.

clue.text: Deal arranged for a Spartan queen

indicators.note: arranged signals that the letters of deal are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A deal is set up on behalf of a queen from Sparta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges DEAL. In Greek myth she was the queen of Sparta seduced by Zeus in the form of a swan.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth she was wife of King Tyndareus of Sparta and mother of Helen.

clue.text: More frivolous, though not so colourful

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both less serious in tone and paler in colour.

clue.text: Junior minister negotiating a truce

indicators.note: negotiating suggests working something out, so the letters of a truce are rearranged

explanation.surface: A government junior minister brokers a ceasefire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Junior minister' suggests a government post, but it is a junior clergyman; 'negotiating' rearranges A TRUCE.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant to a parish priest is a junior minister of the church.

clue.text: Gets even

parts.note: read as taking revenge, but also as making a surface flat or drawing equal

explanation.definitionFit: To make flat or equal is to even something, and to draw level is to get even.

clue.text: She can invariably be taken aback

indicators.note: invariably taken aback says the word is unchanged when read backwards, a palindrome

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A woman who is always ready to be startled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' looks like surprise, but 'invariably be taken aback' says the word reads the same backwards as forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a polite form of address for a woman, so it can stand for she.

clue.text: A name made by writing

parts.note: a name produced by hand-writing it, as at the foot of a letter or cheque

explanation.definitionFit: This is one's own name written by hand to authenticate a document.

clue.text: Trembling, because going to prison

parts.note: as can mean because
pen is slang for a prison, short for penitentiary

explanation.surface: Someone shaking because they are headed for jail.
explanation.walkthrough: The tree's leaves flutter in the slightest breeze, hence the trembling poplar.
explanation.definitionFit: This poplar is known for leaves that quiver, so it is a byword for trembling.

clue.text: One medico finds the French way wet

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
rue is French for street or way

explanation.surface: A single doctor discovers a damp French street.
explanation.walkthrough: MB stands for Bachelor of Medicine, so it serves for a doctor; RUE is the French word for street.
explanation.definitionFit: To soak or stain, especially with blood, is to wet or drench.

clue.text: Sorting post, a boy can cause a hold-up

indicators.note: sorting the post rearranges the letters of that word

parts.note: a page is a boy attendant or servant

explanation.surface: A young lad sorting the mail might cause a delay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sorting' rearranges POST to STOP; a PAGE is a boy servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A halt or blockage in work or flow is a hold-up.

clue.text: Almost see eye to eye on back street addresses

indicators.note: almost means the word is not quite complete, losing a single letter

parts.note: to see eye to eye is to agree

indicators.note: back says the street abbreviation is turned round

explanation.surface: Two people nearly in agreement about the street behind them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops a letter from the front of the agreeing word here, not the usual last letter; 'back' turns the street abbreviation round.
explanation.definitionFit: To greet someone is to address or hail them, a verb sense.

clue.text: Royal lady among many featured in the newspapers

indicators.note: featured in signals that pieces sit inside the newspapers word

parts.note: the press is the newspapers collectively
among can be expressed as in
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword convention for many

explanation.surface: A royal woman who is one of many pictured in the papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'many' is C, the Roman hundred, a common crossword shorthand; 'featured in' puts both pieces inside the newspapers word.
explanation.definitionFit: A king's or queen's daughter is a lady of royal rank.
